category.name: Google Cloud
category.description: Incidents in Google Cloud organizations: IAM and service accounts, Cloud Storage, Compute, GKE, BigQuery, logging, and org policy abuse.

playbooks.name: GCP service account key file leaked
playbooks.summary: Use when a service account JSON key is found in a public repository, paste site, or container image, or Google notifies you that a key was exposed publicly.

preparation: Enforce the iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation org policy except in approved projects
Inventory existing user-managed service account keys with their owners
Route Cloud Audit Logs from all projects to Splunk through a Pub/Sub sink
identification: Record the key ID from private_key_id in the leaked JSON and the service account email
Search audit logs for authenticationInfo.serviceAccountKeyName matching the key ID
Check the Policy Analyzer key usage data for last authentication time of the key
List the IAM roles the service account holds across projects and folders
Identify the source IPs and user agents that used the key since the leak
containment: Disable the leaked key with gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable
Remove high-privilege role bindings from the service account temporarily
Delete any new keys or service accounts created by sessions using the leaked key
eradication: Delete the leaked key after confirming the workload uses a replacement
Remove the key from the repository history and any built container images
Delete resources created by the attacker with the key in every project
recovery: Move the workload to attached service accounts or workload identity federation
Confirm the workload authenticates without the deleted key
Watch audit logs for authentication attempts with the deleted key ID
lessons: Count remaining user-managed keys and set a retirement plan
Add a detection for service account key use from outside known IP ranges
Review why the key was stored where it leaked

splunk.title: Calls authenticated with the leaked key
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.serviceAccountKeyName=*<key_id>* | stats count min(_time) as first values(data.protoPayload.methodName) as methods by data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp, data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerSuppliedUserAgent | convert ctime(first)

splunk.title: Keys and accounts created by the service account
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=<sa_email> data.protoPayload.methodName IN (google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccountKey, google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccount, SetIamPolicy) | table _time data.resource.labels.project_id data.protoPayload.methodName data.protoPayload.resourceName

playbooks.name: Service account impersonation chain to a privileged account
playbooks.summary: Use when a principal uses GenerateAccessToken or signJwt to impersonate service accounts in sequence, reaching one with broader privileges than the original identity.

preparation: Enable Data Access audit logs for IAM Service Account Credentials API
Restrict roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to named principals per service account
Map approved impersonation relationships for automation
identification: List GenerateAccessToken, GenerateIdToken, and SignJwt calls with caller and target service account
Follow the delegation chain in serviceAccountDelegationInfo to the original principal
Compare each hop with the approved impersonation map
List actions taken with the final impersonated token
Check who granted Token Creator on the target service accounts and when
containment: Remove roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator bindings that enabled unexpected hops
Disable the originating user or service account
Disable the privileged target service account if the workload can tolerate it
eradication: Undo IAM and resource changes made by the impersonated tokens
Search for other principals granted Token Creator or Service Account User recently
Remediate the original principal's compromise
recovery: Re-enable the privileged service account with tightened impersonation bindings
Confirm automation pipelines still impersonate along approved paths
Run IAM Recommender to remove unused impersonation grants
lessons: Add a detection for impersonation chains with more than one hop
Audit project-level Token Creator grants that apply to all service accounts
Record which privileged accounts were reachable

splunk.title: Token generation for impersonation
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.serviceName=iamcredentials.googleapis.com data.protoPayload.methodName IN (GenerateAccessToken, GenerateIdToken, SignJwt, SignBlob) | table _time data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.serviceAccountDelegationInfo{}.firstPartyPrincipal.principalEmail data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp

splunk.title: Grants of Token Creator or Service Account User
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName=*SetIamPolicy (data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator OR data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.role=roles/iam.serviceAccountUser) | table _time data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.member

playbooks.name: Cloud Storage bucket made public to allUsers
playbooks.summary: Use when a GCS bucket or object IAM policy grants allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers, or public access prevention is turned off on a bucket holding internal data.

preparation: Enforce storage.publicAccessPrevention org policy on all non-website projects
Enable uniform bucket-level access so object ACLs cannot grant public access
Label buckets with data classification and owning team
identification: Find the storage.setIamPermissions call that added allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers
Check the bucket's publicAccessPrevention setting history
Review Data Access logs for anonymous storage.objects.get calls during exposure
Determine the classification of the exposed objects
Confirm with the bucket owner whether public access was intended
containment: Remove allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers bindings with gcloud storage buckets remove-iam-policy-binding
Set public access prevention to enforced on the bucket
Enable uniform bucket-level access if legacy ACLs were in use
eradication: Rotate any credentials stored in the exposed objects
Remove objects uploaded anonymously if write access was granted
Fix the IaC module or script that produced the public binding
recovery: Serve intentionally public content through a dedicated website project
Confirm Security Command Center shows no PUBLIC_BUCKET_ACL finding
Hand the access log extract to privacy for exposure assessment
lessons: Track exposure duration from binding change to removal
Add an alert on setIamPermissions with allUsers members
Review projects excluded from the public access prevention policy

splunk.title: Bucket IAM changes granting public members
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.serviceName=storage.googleapis.com data.protoPayload.methodName IN (storage.setIamPermissions, storage.buckets.update) (data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.member=allUsers OR data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.member=allAuthenticatedUsers) | table _time data.resource.labels.bucket_name data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.role

splunk.title: Anonymous object reads from the bucket
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName=storage.objects.get data.resource.labels.bucket_name=<bucket> (data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="" OR NOT data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=*) | stats count dc(data.protoPayload.resourceName) as objects by data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp

playbooks.name: Mass download of objects from Cloud Storage
playbooks.summary: Use when a principal reads an unusual number of GCS objects or bytes, or uses gsutil or Storage Transfer Service to copy bucket contents to another project.

preparation: Enable Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage on sensitive projects
Place sensitive projects inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter
Baseline daily object reads per principal for sensitive buckets
identification: Count objects read by the principal per hour and compare with the baseline
Identify caller IPs and whether requests came through the VPC SC perimeter
Check for storagetransfer.googleapis.com jobs created to copy the bucket
Look for storage.objects.list enumeration before the reads
Check for VPC SC violation logs showing blocked copy attempts
containment: Remove the principal's storage roles on the bucket
Disable the principal or its keys if it is a service account
Delete or pause Storage Transfer jobs created by the attacker
eradication: Remediate how the principal's credentials were obtained
Rotate secrets contained in the downloaded objects
Remove any destination bucket bindings the attacker added
recovery: Add the bucket's project to the VPC SC perimeter if it was outside
Provide the data owner a list of objects read
Monitor the principal for continued reads for 30 days
lessons: Add a detection on distinct objects read per principal per hour
Review whether the principal needed bucket-wide read access
Decide whether Storage Transfer Service should be restricted by org policy

splunk.title: Object reads per principal per hour
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName=storage.objects.get data.resource.labels.bucket_name=<bucket> | bin _time span=1h | stats dc(data.protoPayload.resourceName) as objects by _time, data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp | sort - objects

splunk.title: Storage Transfer jobs and VPC SC violations
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message (data.protoPayload.serviceName=storagetransfer.googleapis.com data.protoPayload.methodName=*CreateTransferJob) OR data.protoPayload.metadata.violationReason=* | table _time data.protoPayload.methodName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.metadata.violationReason data.protoPayload.resourceName

playbooks.name: Compute Engine instances launched for cryptomining
playbooks.summary: Use when Security Command Center reports cryptomining, or many high-CPU or GPU Compute Engine instances appear unexpectedly in a project or zone.

preparation: Enable Security Command Center Premium threat detection for the organization
Set GPU and CPU quotas low in projects that do not need them
Configure billing budgets with alerts per project
identification: List compute.instances.insert calls by machine type, zone, and caller
Read instance metadata startup-script values for miner download commands
Check VPC flow logs for egress to mining pool ports
Check whether instance templates or managed instance groups were created to scale the miners
Identify the credential used and how it was obtained
containment: Stop the mining instances after snapshotting their boot disks
Disable the service account or user that created them
Add an egress firewall rule denying mining pool destinations
eradication: Delete the instances, templates, and managed instance groups the attacker created
Remove project-wide SSH keys added to metadata
Sweep every zone and project for attacker resources
recovery: Request a billing adjustment from Google Cloud support with the timeline
Restore reduced quotas in the project
Confirm SCC has no active cryptomining findings
lessons: Add a detection for instance creation with GPU accelerators
Restrict usable regions with gcp.resourceLocations org policy
Measure cost incurred before containment

splunk.title: Instance creation by machine type
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName IN (v1.compute.instances.insert, beta.compute.instances.insert, v1.compute.instanceTemplates.insert, v1.compute.instanceGroupManagers.insert) | rex field=data.protoPayload.request.machineType "machineTypes/(?<machine_type>[^/]+)$" | stats count values(machine_type) as types by data.resource.labels.project_id, data.resource.labels.zone, data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail

splunk.title: Egress to mining pool ports
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false sum(All_Traffic.bytes) as bytes from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444) by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port | sort - bytes

playbooks.name: GCP organization policy constraint removed or relaxed
playbooks.summary: Use when an org policy such as domain-restricted sharing, key creation, or public access prevention is deleted or overridden at the organization, folder, or project level.

preparation: Manage org policies only through a Terraform pipeline with code review
Limit roles/orgpolicy.policyAdmin to the cloud governance team
Alert on SetOrgPolicy, DeleteOrgPolicy, and UpdatePolicy calls
identification: Identify the constraint changed, the resource level, and the caller
Diff the live policy against the Terraform definition
List resources created during the relaxed period that the constraint would have blocked
Check whether the caller also changed IAM on the same folder or project
Confirm whether a change request exists for the override
containment: Reapply the constraint from the pipeline at the original level
Remove the caller's orgpolicy admin role pending review
Revoke tokens for the caller's sessions
eradication: Remove non-compliant resources created while the constraint was relaxed
Delete service account keys or external IAM members added during the window
Remediate the caller's compromised credential if applicable
recovery: Run the policy pipeline in plan mode to confirm no drift
Verify the constraint blocks a test violation
Report final policy state to cloud governance
lessons: Add daily drift detection for org policies
Review who holds policy admin at folder levels
Track the time the constraint was relaxed

splunk.title: Org policy changes
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.serviceName IN (orgpolicy.googleapis.com, cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com) data.protoPayload.methodName IN (*SetOrgPolicy, *ClearOrgPolicy, *CreatePolicy, *UpdatePolicy, *DeletePolicy) | table _time data.protoPayload.methodName data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp

splunk.title: Key creation and external IAM during the relaxed window
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message earliest=<change_time> data.protoPayload.methodName IN (google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccountKey, SetIamPolicy) | table _time data.resource.labels.project_id data.protoPayload.methodName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.member

playbooks.name: Cloud Logging sink deleted or audit logs excluded
playbooks.summary: Use when a log sink exporting audit logs is deleted or updated, an exclusion filter drops audit entries, or the _Default bucket retention is reduced.

preparation: Use an aggregated organization sink to a locked log bucket in a security project
Lock the destination log bucket's retention policy
Alert when the Pub/Sub subscription feeding Splunk stops delivering messages
identification: Identify the DeleteSink, UpdateSink, or exclusion change and its caller
Compare the sink filter before and after any update
Determine which projects and log types stopped flowing and for how long
Check the _Required bucket, which cannot be disabled, for admin activity in the gap
Look for Data Access audit config changes via SetIamPolicy auditConfigs
containment: Recreate the sink with the original filter and destination
Remove the exclusion filter that dropped audit entries
Revoke the caller's logging admin roles
eradication: Reconstruct the gap from the _Required bucket and the locked central bucket
Undo changes the attacker made during the gap
Re-grant the sink writer identity permission on the destination
recovery: Confirm audit entries from all projects reach Splunk again
Restore Data Access audit log configuration on affected services
Document any unrecoverable log gap
lessons: Restrict logging.sinks.delete with a custom role and deny policy
Add a delivery-latency monitor on the Splunk Pub/Sub subscription
Measure time to detect the log gap

splunk.title: Sink, exclusion, and bucket changes
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.serviceName=logging.googleapis.com data.protoPayload.methodName IN (google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink, google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink, google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.CreateExclusion, google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateExclusion, google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateBucket, google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSettings) | table _time data.protoPayload.methodName data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.request

splunk.title: Projects that stopped sending audit logs
splunk.spl: | tstats max(_time) as last_seen where index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message by data.resource.labels.project_id | where last_seen < relative_time(now(), "-2h") | convert ctime(last_seen)

playbooks.name: Owner or Editor role granted to an external account
playbooks.summary: Use when SetIamPolicy grants roles/owner, roles/editor, or other admin roles on a project, folder, or organization to a gmail.com or non-corporate identity.

preparation: Enforce iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains to restrict members to the corporate Workspace customer ID
Alert on SetIamPolicy binding deltas that add basic roles
Keep an approved list of vendor domains with project access
identification: Extract the member, role, and resource from the policyDelta binding deltas
Check the member domain against corporate and approved vendor domains
Identify who made the grant and from which IP
Search for activity by the external member after the grant
Check whether domain-restricted sharing was overridden on the resource
containment: Remove the external member's binding with remove-iam-policy-binding
Disable the granting principal if the grant was unauthorized
Reapply domain-restricted sharing on the resource
eradication: Remove resources, keys, or service accounts created by the external member
Search all projects for other bindings to the same external identity
Remediate the granting principal's compromise
recovery: Confirm the project IAM policy matches its Terraform state
Run Policy Analyzer to confirm the external identity has no remaining access
Inform the project owner of the final IAM state
lessons: Add a detection for any SetIamPolicy member ending in gmail.com
Review why basic roles are still used on this project
Measure time from grant to removal

splunk.title: Admin roles granted to non-corporate members
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName=*SetIamPolicy | spath path=data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{} output=delta | mvexpand delta | spath input=delta | search action=ADD role IN (roles/owner, roles/editor, roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin, roles/iam.securityAdmin) NOT member=*@<corp_domain> | table _time data.protoPayload.resourceName role member data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail

splunk.title: Actions by the external member
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=<external_member> | stats count values(data.protoPayload.methodName) as methods by data.resource.labels.project_id, data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp

playbooks.name: GKE cluster compromised through workload or API access
playbooks.summary: Use when a GKE workload is exploited, an unexpected identity gains cluster-admin, privileged pods are created, or the Kubernetes API is reached from an unknown network.

preparation: Enable GKE Security Posture and Container Threat Detection
Use private clusters with authorized networks on the control plane
Enable GKE Workload Identity and disable legacy metadata endpoints
identification: Review Kubernetes audit logs for clusterrolebindings created to cluster-admin
List pods created with privileged, hostPID, or hostPath mounts
Check exec and attach calls into running pods by user and source IP
Identify the vulnerable workload and its image digest
Check whether the node service account token was used outside the cluster
containment: Apply a deny-all NetworkPolicy to the compromised namespace
Delete rogue clusterrolebindings and service account tokens
Restrict master authorized networks to the admin network range
eradication: Delete attacker-created pods, DaemonSets, and CronJobs
Recreate node pools that ran privileged attacker pods
Patch or replace the exploited workload image
recovery: Redeploy workloads from signed images with Binary Authorization enforced
Rotate cluster credentials with gcloud container clusters update --start-credential-rotation
Confirm Container Threat Detection shows no new findings
lessons: Enforce Pod Security Admission restricted profile on application namespaces
Add a detection for cluster-admin bindings outside GitOps
Review whether the public control plane endpoint was necessary

splunk.title: RBAC and privileged workload changes in GKE
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.resource.type=k8s_cluster data.protoPayload.methodName IN (io.k8s.authorization.rbac.v1.clusterrolebindings.create, io.k8s.authorization.rbac.v1.rolebindings.create, io.k8s.core.v1.pods.create, io.k8s.apps.v1.daemonsets.create, io.k8s.batch.v1.cronjobs.create) | table _time data.resource.labels.cluster_name data.protoPayload.methodName data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp

splunk.title: Exec into pods
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.resource.type=k8s_cluster data.protoPayload.methodName IN (io.k8s.core.v1.pods.exec.create, io.k8s.core.v1.pods.attach.create) | stats count by data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, data.protoPayload.resourceName, data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp

playbooks.name: Cloud Functions or Cloud Run service backdoored
playbooks.summary: Use when a Cloud Function or Cloud Run service is deployed or updated by an unexpected principal, gains allUsers invoker access, or runs with a privileged service account.

preparation: Deploy functions and Cloud Run services only from Cloud Build with a dedicated service account
Give each function a dedicated runtime service account instead of the default compute account
Record the source archive hash and image digest for each release
identification: List CreateFunction, UpdateFunction, and Cloud Run ReplaceService calls by principal
Compare the deployed source or image digest with the last release record
Check SetIamPolicy for roles/cloudfunctions.invoker or roles/run.invoker granted to allUsers
Identify the runtime service account and its roles
Review the function's logs for outbound calls or token requests
containment: Remove allUsers invoker bindings from the function or service
Roll traffic back to the last known-good revision
Disable the deploying principal pending review
eradication: Delete attacker-created functions, services, and Eventarc triggers
Redeploy from the trusted Cloud Build pipeline
Rotate secrets the runtime service account could access
recovery: Confirm revisions and digests match the release record
Assign a least-privilege runtime service account
Watch invocation logs for unusual callers for two weeks
lessons: Add a detection for allUsers invoker grants
Enforce the iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts org policy
Review which humans can deploy production functions

splunk.title: Function and Cloud Run deployments
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.serviceName IN (cloudfunctions.googleapis.com, run.googleapis.com) data.protoPayload.methodName IN (*CreateFunction, *UpdateFunction, *CreateService, *ReplaceService, *UpdateService) | table _time data.protoPayload.methodName data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp

splunk.title: Public invoker grants
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName=*SetIamPolicy data.protoPayload.serviceName IN (cloudfunctions.googleapis.com, run.googleapis.com) data.protoPayload.serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas{}.member=allUsers | table _time data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail

playbooks.name: Access token stolen from the GCE metadata server
playbooks.summary: Use when an SSRF or compromised workload reads service account tokens from metadata.google.internal and those tokens are used from outside the instance or for unusual APIs.

preparation: Attach least-privilege service accounts to instances instead of the default compute account
Avoid the cloud-platform access scope on instances that do not need it
Log application requests with full URLs so SSRF payloads are visible
identification: Search web logs for requests containing metadata.google.internal or 169.254.169.254
Check whether the vulnerable code path lets the caller set the Metadata-Flavor: Google header
Find audit log calls by the instance service account from caller IPs not belonging to the instance
List APIs and resources accessed with the stolen token
Identify the vulnerable application endpoint and parameter
containment: Remove the instance service account's high-privilege role bindings
Stop the instance or block the vulnerable endpoint at Cloud Armor
Disable the service account if other workloads do not depend on it
eradication: Patch the application's URL fetching to allowlist destinations
Remove resources or IAM changes made with the stolen token
Replace the default compute service account with a dedicated account
recovery: Re-enable the service account after access tokens have expired and the fix is deployed
Confirm no further use of the account from external IPs
Add SSRF regression tests to the application's CI
lessons: Add a detection for instance service account use from non-GCP IPs
Count instances using the default compute service account with Editor
Review Cloud Armor rules for SSRF patterns

splunk.title: Requests targeting the metadata server
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*metadata.google.internal*" OR Web.url="*169.254.169.254*" OR Web.url="*computeMetadata*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url | sort - count

splunk.title: Instance service account used from unexpected IPs
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=<instance_sa> NOT data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp IN (<instance_ips>) | stats count values(data.protoPayload.methodName) as methods by data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp, data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerSuppliedUserAgent

playbooks.name: BigQuery dataset exfiltrated by export or copy
playbooks.summary: Use when a principal runs large extract jobs, copies tables into another project, shares a dataset externally, or queries far more data than usual from sensitive BigQuery datasets.

preparation: Place BigQuery projects with sensitive data inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter
Tag sensitive datasets with policy tags for column-level security
Baseline bytes processed per principal per day
identification: List jobservice.jobcompleted events with extract or copy jobs and their destinations
Check destination tables and GCS URIs for projects outside the organization
Rank principals by totalBilledBytes on the sensitive datasets
Check dataset IAM changes adding external members or allAuthenticatedUsers
Review VPC SC violation logs for blocked BigQuery egress
containment: Remove the principal's BigQuery data viewer roles on the dataset
Remove external members from the dataset access list
Cancel running extract or copy jobs with bq cancel
eradication: Delete in-org copies of the data created by the attacker
Remediate the principal's credential compromise
Revoke authorized views or routines that exposed the dataset
recovery: Bring the project into the VPC SC perimeter if it was outside
Provide the data owner a list of tables and columns accessed
Engage privacy for breach assessment if personal data was exported
lessons: Add a detection on extract jobs to buckets outside the organization
Review whether analysts need table-wide export rights
Measure volume exported before containment

splunk.title: BigQuery extract and copy jobs
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.serviceName=bigquery.googleapis.com data.protoPayload.methodName=jobservice.jobcompleted (data.protoPayload.serviceData.jobCompletedEvent.job.jobConfiguration.extract.destinationUris{}=* OR data.protoPayload.serviceData.jobCompletedEvent.job.jobConfiguration.tableCopy.destinationTable.projectId=*) | table _time data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail data.protoPayload.serviceData.jobCompletedEvent.job.jobConfiguration.extract.destinationUris{} data.protoPayload.serviceData.jobCompletedEvent.job.jobConfiguration.tableCopy.destinationTable.projectId

splunk.title: Top principals by bytes billed
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName=jobservice.jobcompleted | eval bytes=tonumber('data.protoPayload.serviceData.jobCompletedEvent.job.jobStatistics.totalBilledBytes') | stats sum(bytes) as bytes count by data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail | eval GB=round(bytes/1024/1024/1024,1) | sort - bytes

playbooks.name: VPC firewall rule opened to 0.0.0.0/0
playbooks.summary: Use when a VPC firewall rule allows ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to SSH, RDP, database, or all ports, exposing Compute Engine or GKE nodes to the internet.

preparation: Provide Identity-Aware Proxy TCP forwarding for administrative access
Use hierarchical firewall policies to deny internet ingress on admin ports
Enable VPC flow logs and firewall rules logging on production subnets
identification: Identify the firewall rule, ports, target tags, and creator from audit logs
List instances matching the rule's target tags or service accounts
Review firewall rule logs for allowed connections from internet sources
Check exposed hosts for successful logins or exploitation during exposure
Ask the creator whether the rule was intended as temporary
containment: Delete or disable the rule with gcloud compute firewall-rules update --disabled
Replace it with an IAP source range 35.235.240.0/20 rule if access is needed
Isolate hosts showing signs of compromise by removing their network tags
eradication: Investigate compromised hosts for persistence and rebuild them
Rotate credentials on exposed database or admin services
Fix the Terraform module or script that created the rule
recovery: Move administrators to IAP-based SSH
Confirm SCC shows no OPEN_FIREWALL findings for the project
Monitor firewall logs for continued inbound attempts
lessons: Add a hierarchical policy denying 0.0.0.0/0 on admin ports organization-wide
Record the exposure duration and connection count
Add an alert on firewall rules with sourceRanges 0.0.0.0/0

splunk.title: Firewall rules opened to the internet
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.protoPayload.methodName IN (v1.compute.firewalls.insert, v1.compute.firewalls.patch, v1.compute.firewalls.update) data.protoPayload.request.sourceRanges{}="0.0.0.0/0" | table _time data.resource.labels.project_id data.protoPayload.resourceName data.protoPayload.request.alloweds{}.ports{} data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail

splunk.title: Allowed internet connections on the rule
splunk.spl: index=gcp sourcetype=google:gcp:pubsub:message data.jsonPayload.rule_details.reference=*<rule_name>* data.jsonPayload.disposition=ALLOWED | stats count dc(data.jsonPayload.connection.src_ip) as sources by data.jsonPayload.connection.dest_ip, data.jsonPayload.connection.dest_port

playbooks.name: Unauthorized GCP project created for abuse
playbooks.summary: Use when a new project appears in the organization or under a billing account without a request, often used to run compute, AI services, or staging infrastructure outside normal controls.

preparation: Remove roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator from the domain-wide default grant
Require new projects to be created through a project factory pipeline
Restrict roles/billing.user on billing accounts to the project factory
identification: Identify the CreateProject call, creator, parent folder, and source IP
Check whether a billing account was linked with UpdateProjectBillingInfo
List APIs enabled in the project with services.enable calls
Enumerate resources created in the project, such as instances or Vertex AI endpoints
Check whether the creator is a compromised user or service account
containment: Unlink billing from the project with gcloud billing projects unlink
Remove the creator's projectCreator and billing roles
Move the project into a quarantine folder with deny policies
eradication: Shut down the project with gcloud projects delete after evidence capture
Remove any IAM bindings granting external identities access to the project
Search for other projects created by the same principal
recovery: Request billing review for charges incurred by the project
Confirm the project is in DELETE_REQUESTED state
Verify the project factory remains the only creator
lessons: Add an alert for CreateProject by principals other than the project factory
Review the organization-level IAM for broad project creation rights
Measure charges incurred before detection

playbooks.name: Unusual access to Secret Manager secret versions
playbooks.summary: Use when a principal calls AccessSecretVersion on many secrets or on secrets it never used before, indicating credential harvesting from Secret Manager.

preparation: Enable Data Access audit logs for secretmanager.googleapis.com
Grant roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor per secret rather than at project level
Label secrets with the owning application and rotation contact
identification: Count distinct secrets accessed by the principal and compare with prior weeks
Check whether ListSecrets enumeration preceded the access calls
Identify caller IPs and whether they belong to the workload's runtime
List the downstream systems each secret grants access to
Check for PERMISSION_DENIED accesses showing probing beyond granted scope
containment: Remove project-level secretAccessor bindings from the principal
Disable the principal or its service account keys
Disable the accessed secret versions after new versions are added
eradication: Rotate each accessed secret and update consuming applications
Check downstream systems for logins using the harvested credentials
Remediate the principal's compromise
recovery: Destroy the old secret versions once consumers use the new ones
Configure rotation schedules and Pub/Sub notifications on critical secrets
Monitor the principal's secret access for 30 days
lessons: Add a detection on distinct AccessSecretVersion per principal per hour
Replace project-level accessor grants with per-secret grants
Measure time to rotate all exposed secrets

playbooks.name: Cloud SQL instance exposed with public IP and open networks
playbooks.summary: Use when a Cloud SQL instance gains a public IP with authorized networks of 0.0.0.0/0, SSL enforcement is removed, or the instance is exported to an unknown bucket.

preparation: Enforce sql.restrictPublicIp and sql.restrictAuthorizedNetworks org policies
Use Cloud SQL Auth Proxy or private service access for application connections
Enable Cloud SQL database audit flags such as pgaudit or the MySQL audit plugin
identification: Find cloudsql.instances.update calls that set ipv4Enabled or added authorizedNetworks
Check whether requireSsl or sslMode was relaxed in the same change
Review database logs for logins from internet addresses during the exposure
Check for cloudsql.instances.export calls and the destination bucket
Identify which database users have weak or default passwords
containment: Remove 0.0.0.0/0 from authorized networks and disable the public IP
Re-enable SSL-only connections on the instance
Revoke the caller's cloudsql.admin role pending review
eradication: Rotate database user passwords, starting with the postgres or root user
Delete database users created by an attacker
Remove exported dump files from any bucket the attacker controlled or used
recovery: Reconnect applications through the Auth Proxy or private IP
Confirm SCC shows no PUBLIC_SQL_INSTANCE or SQL_NO_ROOT_PASSWORD findings
Review query logs for data access during the exposure window
lessons: Add an alert on authorizedNetworks changes containing 0.0.0.0/0
Review why the org policy did not apply to this project
Measure the exposure window

playbooks.name: Cloud KMS key version destroyed or disabled
playbooks.summary: Use when DestroyCryptoKeyVersion or disable calls target a Cloud KMS key protecting CMEK data, or the key's IAM policy grants decrypt access to an unknown principal.

preparation: Set a long scheduled destruction duration on key rings holding CMEK keys
Keep Cloud KMS keys in a dedicated security project with restricted IAM
Map each CMEK key to the BigQuery, GCS, Compute, and SQL resources it protects
identification: Identify the key version, caller, and scheduled destroy time from the audit event
Check whether versions were disabled before the destroy request
Diff the key's IAM policy for new cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter grantees
List workloads failing with key-unavailable errors
Determine whether the key is imported material or Cloud EKM
containment: Restore the key version with gcloud kms keys versions restore before destruction completes
Re-enable the key version with gcloud kms keys versions enable
Remove unauthorized IAM bindings from the key
eradication: Revoke the caller's cloudkms.admin role and investigate its compromise
Remove other destroy or disable requests the attacker scheduled
Check other key rings in the project for similar changes
recovery: Confirm CMEK-protected resources can read data again
Verify automatic rotation settings on the key are unchanged
Document which data would have been lost if destruction completed
lessons: Separate KMS admin from key usage roles so no one holds both
Add a detection for DestroyCryptoKeyVersion on any key
Review the minimum destroy-scheduled duration org policy

playbooks.name: Workload identity federation abused by an external identity
playbooks.summary: Use when a workload identity pool provider accepts tokens from an unexpected repository, tenant, or issuer, letting an external identity impersonate a GCP service account.

preparation: Set an attribute condition on every provider restricting repository, ref, or tenant
Bind workloadIdentityUser to specific principal:// subjects rather than whole pools
Enable Data Access logs for sts.googleapis.com and iamcredentials.googleapis.com
identification: Review sts.googleapis.com ExchangeToken events for the provider and mapped subject
Compare the subject and attributes with the approved repositories or tenants
Check for CreateWorkloadIdentityPoolProvider or UpdateWorkloadIdentityPoolProvider changes
Follow the federated token to GenerateAccessToken on target service accounts
List actions taken by the impersonated service account during the session
containment: Disable the workload identity pool provider
Remove principalSet bindings that grant the whole pool access to service accounts
Revert the provider's issuer or attribute condition to the approved values
eradication: Undo resource and IAM changes made by the impersonated service account
Remove rogue pools or providers created by the attacker
Rotate secrets the service account could read
recovery: Re-enable the provider with a strict attribute condition and test the approved pipeline
Confirm no ExchangeToken events from unapproved subjects
Document the approved subject list in the provider's description
lessons: Audit every provider for missing attribute conditions
Add a detection for ExchangeToken from unknown subjects
Review who can modify workload identity pools

playbooks.name: GCP billing anomaly from unexpected services or regions
playbooks.summary: Use when a budget alert or cost anomaly shows sudden spend on Compute, GPUs, Vertex AI, or egress in projects or regions that do not normally incur it.

preparation: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery for daily per-SKU analysis
Set budgets with Pub/Sub notifications on every billing account and key project
Restrict resource locations with the gcp.resourceLocations org policy
identification: Query the billing export grouped by project, service, SKU, and location for the spike
Correlate the top SKUs with resource creation calls in audit logs
Check for Vertex AI or Generative AI API usage from unknown principals
Check for large internet egress SKUs that could signal data exfiltration
Identify the principals and credentials behind the costly resources
containment: Disable the principals creating the costly resources
Stop or delete the resources driving the spend after capturing metadata
Disable abused APIs in the project with gcloud services disable
eradication: Remove persistence such as instance templates or scheduled jobs that recreate resources
Rotate API keys and service account keys used in the abuse
Restrict quotas for the abused services
recovery: Open a billing support case with the incident timeline
Confirm daily spend returns to baseline in the billing export
Re-enable APIs needed by legitimate workloads
lessons: Add budget alerts at lower thresholds for projects with stable spend
Restrict API key usage with application and API restrictions
Measure cost between first anomalous charge and containment

playbooks.name: Poisoned container image pushed to Artifact Registry
playbooks.summary: Use when an Artifact Registry image tag or package is overwritten by an unexpected principal, or a repository grants public or external write access.

preparation: Enable immutable tags on production Artifact Registry repositories
Enforce Binary Authorization attestations for GKE and Cloud Run deployments
Restrict artifactregistry.writer to the Cloud Build service account
identification: List docker push or UploadArtifact calls on the repository by principal and IP
Compare the tag's current digest with the digest attested at the last release
Pull the suspect digest in an isolated environment and diff its layers
Check repository IAM for allUsers readers or external writers
Find GKE and Cloud Run workloads running the suspect digest
containment: Pin workloads to the last attested digest and redeploy
Remove the pushing principal's writer role
Remove external or public bindings from the repository
eradication: Delete the poisoned version after preserving a copy as evidence
Investigate workloads that ran the poisoned image for credential access
Rotate secrets mounted into those workloads
recovery: Rebuild the image from source in Cloud Build and attest it
Confirm Binary Authorization blocks the poisoned digest
Run Artifact Analysis vulnerability scanning on the rebuilt image
lessons: Move Binary Authorization from dry-run to enforce mode
Add a detection for pushes by principals other than Cloud Build
Record how many workloads ran the poisoned digest
